chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Ma'shah) from Al-Abbas from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah from Abu Al-Jarud who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): We were uncertain for a year in one of those years regarding the sacrifice (Al-Adha) - so when I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and some of our companions were sacrificing, he said: 'The breaking of the fast (Al-Fitr) is the day when people break their fast, and the sacrifice (Al-Adha) is the day when people sacrifice, and the fasting is the day when people fast.'

key_terms.الشَّكَّ: Uncertainty or doubt, specifically regarding moon sighting
key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: Eid al-Adha, the Festival of Sacrifice
key_terms.الْفِطْرُ: Eid al-Fitr, the Festival of Breaking the Fast

ai.seo_question: How is the date of Eid al-Adha determined according to Shia jurisprudence when the moon is not visible?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of 'following the people' (ittiba' al-nas) for determining the dates of Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, and fasting, particularly in cases of uncertainty regarding moon sighting. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential reliance on communal consensus and practical observation over rigid fixed calendars, ensuring religious observances align with the general Muslim community's actions. This ruling highlights the flexibility within Shia fiqh to accommodate natural variations in lunar visibility while maintaining unity in worship.
